source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Tune Up, p.6-3

procedures.title: Spark plugs: service and install
steps: Be very careful with the tap not to cross-thread; crank the engine several times afterward to blow out loosened material.
Fit the plugs with new gaskets and torque to specifications.
notes: Common causes of poor plug performance: too little torque to seat the gasket fully, too much torque (changes the gap), installing on a dirty gasket seat, and installing into corroded threads.

procedures.title: Ignition system: service
steps: Take off the distributor cap, clean it and check for cracks, carbon tracks and burned or corroded terminals; replace if needed.
Clean the rotor and check for damage or wear; replace if needed.
Replace brittle, oil-soaked or damaged plug wires and route each to the correct plug; seat the wires properly in their supports to avoid cross-firing.
Repair or replace frayed, loose or damaged wires.

procedures.title: Magnetic pulse (breakerless) distributor: maintenance
steps: No periodic maintenance is needed; the amplifier has no moving parts and the distributor shaft and bushings are permanently lubricated.
For problems and repair of the transistorized magnetic pulse system, see Section 6Y.

procedures.title: Breaker point distributor: service
steps: Test the centrifugal advance: turn the rotor clockwise as far as it goes and release it; the springs must return it to the retarded position, otherwise take the distributor apart and fix the cause.
Test the vacuum spark control: turn the movable breaker plate counterclockwise and check that the spring returns it to retarded; correct any binding, since stiffness changes ignition timing.
Inspect the points and clean or replace them as needed (see figure 4 in the manual for the V8 distributor and figure 5 for point alignment).
